findings.text: §13 says the stalled row "appears in its coordinator's obligations", but the obligations rows the hook reads on a fresh snapshot are built by the published slice in `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1367` (and the earlier slice at `:1277`), both of which call `obligations._queued_item(row, placements=..., now=...)` and are outside s13's declared write paths (`obligations.py`, `needs_you.py`, `queue_admission.py`, `runs.py`, new test); `_queued_item` is called three times per build across two modules, so the done-when's "reads the verdict log once per obligations build" arm cannot hold without threading one build-scoped verdict read into both slice call sites

findings.reason: deleting the module fails those six files at head while leaving it keeps tests on a module with no production caller, so the node cannot satisfy both clauses and must be told which it owns (delete the module and its tests, or keep the module and only drop its stall rows).
findings.text: the deliverable says "remove the stall rows from `needs_you.py`, and the module itself if nothing else calls it", while the done-when requires that "the test files importing `reckon.crew.needs_you` add no failure against the base revision"; six existing test files import the module (`tests/test_a_deferred_run_leaves_the_needs_you_line.py:23`, `tests/test_follow_needs_you_line.py:33`, `tests/test_the_pane_carries_counts_not_names.py:43`, `tests/test_a_pane_settles_when_no_work_is_live.py`, `tests/test_the_stream_carries_only_actionable_lines.py`, `tests/test_follow_drain_line.py`), and none is in the write paths

findings.text: a new row kind must be classified as blocking or non-blocking and §13 does not say which: `obligations.NON_BLOCKING_DUTY_KINDS` (`obligations.py:152`) governs the derivation, while `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:240-242` mirrors that vocabulary as a literal `_NON_BLOCKING_KINDS` set that cannot be imported on the fresh-snapshot path, and the hook is not among the write paths
